## Summary

Prevent book-producing Kinozal feeds through an operator-managed readable denylist, not an allowed-category list or numeric policy in Python.

`KINOZAL_EXCLUDED_CATEGORIES` is a semicolon-separated, case-insensitive GitHub repository variable. Production now contains `Избранные раздачи;Топ Музыки;Библиотека;Избранные аудиокниги;Избранные программы`. Parent entries cover canonical child paths, so `Топ Музыки` also excludes `Топ Музыки > Русская`.

The listing response's selected readable name is authoritative. A match stops before extraction, trailer lookup, and Telegram; every other category processes regardless of numeric ID. Empty, stale, or unparseable category evidence fails open so a future film category cannot be silently suppressed, while configuration failures remain visible. Numeric ID, readable name, and listing URL are retained as provenance.

`KINOZAL_EXCLUDED_GENRES` remains the independent details-page genre filter.

Closes #506

## Risk & Rollback

- Blast radius: Kinozal listing intake, category configuration, provenance, logging, and Actions wiring. Genre filtering, dedup, trailer selection, delivery, and mirror failover are unchanged.
- Availability policy: only readable names explicitly present in the variable are denied. Numeric IDs never suppress items.
- Configuration safety: empty or stale values make the result visibly non-ok but process fail-open.
- Rollback: revert `f414258` and `b442b5a` in a PR, then restore the prior variable/code contract. Do not reintroduce mixed `t=0` into production while numeric filtering is absent.
- Monitoring: investigate configuration errors or selector-evidence warnings; both mean filtering evidence was incomplete, not that an unlisted film category was suppressed.
